decision_rule: Route fixed-line internet and landline faults to Ogero when line or area is known.
examples: internet ma fi b beirut; landline down; Ogero DSL cuts

decision_rule: Ask for municipality exact location or line/account details before field routing.
notes: Fixed telecom faults need location or line context.

decision_rule: Do not route mobile network issues to Ogero. If Alfa or Touch is named use the seeded operator-first channel then TRA for escalation when provider handling fails.
examples: alfa signal down; touch 4g no coverage
notes: Use mobile_operator_channels.csv for Alfa and Touch first-line channels.

decision_rule: Use TRA for regulatory escalation when provider complaint failed or mobile billing dispute is clear.
examples: Alfa bill wrong; roaming overcharge; shakkait ma hallou
notes: TRA is consumer escalation/regulator not first-line technical dispatch.

decision_rule: Do not auto-route private router device or Wi-Fi password issues to Ogero unless public line fault evidence exists.
examples: router password not working; my laptop has no wifi

decision_rule: Confirm provider and whether Ogero last-mile infrastructure is implicated before routing.
examples: private ISP down; Starlink problem; neighborhood cable provider
notes: Private services are outside direct Ogero fixed-line fault unless Ogero asset is involved.

decision_rule: Route Ogero asset repair to Ogero and co-note municipality if public-space obstruction exists.
examples: Ogero cabinet open; internet cable cut in street
notes: Needs exact street location and photo if safe.

decision_rule: Emergency services first if there is immediate danger then Ogero for telecom asset repair.
examples: pole fell on road; cable causing accident risk
notes: Use only for immediate public danger not routine cable damage.
